chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Qāsim narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I buy a bondwoman from a trustworthy man, and he informs me that he has not touched her since she menstruated in his possession and then became pure.

He عليه السلام said: It is not permissible for you to have intercourse with her until you ensure her freedom from pregnancy by one menstrual cycle. But what is short of the private part is permissible for you.
Indeed, those who purchase bondwomen and then have intercourse with them before performing istibrāʾ regarding them—those are adulterers by means of their wealth.

key_terms.الزُّنَاةُ: those described as adulterers due to violating this ruling
key_terms.الْإِمَاءَ: female slaves or bondwomen in the plural
key_terms.الْجَارِيَةَ: a female slave or bondwoman being purchased
key_terms.الْفَرْجِ: the private part, meaning intercourse is excluded
key_terms.الْمَأْمُونِ: a person considered trustworthy in reporting her condition
key_terms.بِحَيْضَةٍ: by one menstrual cycle, the required waiting sign here
key_terms.تَسْتَبْرِئَهَا: to perform istibrāʾ, ensuring she is free of pregnancy before intercourse

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to have intercourse with a purchased bondwoman before istibrāʾ?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling that a purchased bondwoman may not be approached for intercourse until one menstrual cycle has passed as istibrāʾ. It permits non-intercourse intimacy short of the private part and strongly condemns ignoring this ruling as a grave sexual transgression.
